{{Short description|Genus of plesiosaur}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range = [[Middle Jurassic]]
(early [[Bajocian]]), ~{{fossilrange|170}} | image = Gondwananectes osvaldoi (holotype, MUHNCAL.20173).png | image_caption = Holotype material as preserved (A) and tentatively arranged in life position (B) | display_parents = 2 | genus = Gondwananectes | parent_authority = Otero et al., [[2026 in reptile paleontology|2026]] | species = osvaldoi | authority = Otero et al., 2026 }} '''''Gondwananectes''''' ({{lit|[[Gondwana]] swimmer}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[plesiosauroid]] plesiosaur known from the [[Middle Jurassic]] ([[Bajocian]] age) [[Quehuita Formation]] of Chile. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Gondwananectes osvaldoi''''', known from a partial skeleton. == Discovery and naming == The ''Gondwananectes'' fossil material was discovered by Osvaldo Rojas, who collected it with a team of paleontologists in 2014. The bones were found at the {{gloss|Ojo Opache locality}}, representing outcrops of the [[Quehuita Formation]], a site situated {{convert|10|km|mi}} west of [[Calama, Chile|Calama]] in [[Antofagasta Region]], northern Chile. The specimen was found in several scattered fragments, which were transferred to the Museum of Natural and Cultural History of the Atacama Desert in Chile (MUHNCAL), where it is now is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as MUHNCAL.20173. In 2020, Rodrigo A. Otero and colleagues published a preliminary report of the specimen, noting it as the first Middle Jurassic plesiosaur found in that region. They identified it as a possible member of the plesiosaur [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Rhomaleosauridae]] based on putative pelvic bones with apparent similarities to those of the [[Early Jurassic]] ''[[Lindwurmia]]'' of Germany. Additional [[Fossil preparation|preparation]] by Otero between late 2024 and early 2025 allowed for improved study of the material, and revealed that these {{gloss|pelvic bones}} were actually part of the [[pectoral girdle]]. Full preparation revealed that the extent of preserved material comprises several articulated cervical (neck) vertebrae and partial pectoral and dorsal (trunk) vertebrae, several ribs and [[gastralia]]], part of the pectoral girdle ([[coracoid]]s and [[scapula]]e), and badly damaged bones that may be part of the [[Ilium bone|ilium]] (a pelvic bone). In 2026, Otero and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Gondwananectes osvaldoi'' as a new genus and species of early plesiosauroid plesiosaurs based on these fossil remains, establishing MUHNCAL.20173 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Gondwananectes'', combines {{gloss|[[Gondwana]]}}, the ancient southern [[supercontinent]], with the [[Greek language|Greek]] word {{lang|grc|nēktēs}} (a common plesiosaur name suffix), meaning {{gloss|swimmer}}. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''osvaldoi'', honors Osvaldo Rojas, the discoverer of the holotype and director of MUHNCAL. == Description == As preserved, the articulated cervical and dorsal vertebrae measure about {{convert|30|cm|in}} long. Based on the postulated pelvic girdle morphology, the trunk region likely measured {{cvt|60|cm|in}}. Similarly, the humerus size implies a {{cvt|60|-|70|cm|in}}-long forelimb. Based on comparisons with closely related plesiosauroids, ''Gondwananectes'' likely had around 29–39 cervical vertebrae adn 20–23 dorsal vertebrae. In combination, the total body length was likely between {{cvt|1.5|and|2|m|ft}}. Based on some degree of vertebral fusion in the holotype individual, it was not an especially young animal when it died. It was likely a subadult, nearing maturity. == Classification == [[File:Franconiasaurus Life Restoration.jpg|thumb|[[Life restoration]] of the more [[Basal (phylogenetics)|basal]] ''Franconiasaurus'']] To test the affinities and relationships of ''Gondwananectes'', Otero et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of O'Gorman et al. (2024).{{Cite journal |last1=O'Gorman |first1=Jose P. |last2=Canale |first2=Juan I. |last3=Bona |first3=Paula |last4=Tineo |first4=David E. |last5=Reguero |first5=Marcelo |last6=Cárdenas |first6=Magalí |date=2024-12-31 |title=A new elasmosaurid (Plesiosauria: Sauropterygia) from the López de Bertodano Formation: new data on the evolution of the aristonectine morphology |journal=[[Journal of Systematic Palaeontology]] |language=en |volume=22 |issue=1 |doi=10.1080/14772019.2024.2312302 |bibcode=2024JSPal..2212302O |issn=1477-2019}} This dataset recovered ''Gondwananectes'' as a member of the plesiosaur clade [[Plesiosauroidea]], diverging after ''[[Franconiasaurus]]'', as the [[sister taxon]] to the more [[Derived (phylogenetics)|derived]] clade [[Cryptoclidia]].
